decision.summary: The washing machine fix failed after about 5 days. I reopened the job, asked Lantern Services to return at no charge under their workmanship guarantee, and held their invoice. The tenant and landlord have been told, and a follow-up is set for 7 March.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: It was closed on 28 Feb without tenant confirmation, and has now been reopened. The return visit date is outstanding from the provider, and the invoice is on hold.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Ask Lantern Services by email for a no-charge return visit and a confirmed date. The tenant and landlord have also been updated by email.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: No. This is a routine guarantee return visit. A human is only needed if the provider disputes the guarantee or chargeable work arises.

conflicts: The ticket was closed at event 031 although the landlord confirmation was still needed (event 030) and the tenant never confirmed the fix.
The invoice due date (22 July 2026) in event 024 is implausible.
The visit was recorded as 23/02 3.25pm, while the tenant call mentioned Tuesday 1pm.
The ticket reference in the system is NBL-042-repair-failed-recurs, while the emails say NBL-042.

args.body: Dear Lantern Services, the tenant at Flat 20, 120 Alder Lane reports the washing machine fault has returned: your repair (heating element wiring, reported 28 Feb) worked for a couple of washes, but for the last 5 days the water has not heated on the 60°C cycle. Please treat this as a return visit under your workmanship guarantee at no extra charge. Please contact the tenant (details as on the original job email, 07700 900566, enter the code when calling) and confirm a date to us by reply. Please report what you find, and tell us before doing any chargeable work. Your invoice of £75.11 is on hold until this is resolved.
